## Current State

`skills/dispatch/mcp-transport.md` documents the GitHub MCP transport dispatch uses when `gh` is absent or GraphQL-blocked, including required workarounds for several known gaps (label truncation, no generic GraphQL passthrough, etc.). It does not document that `mcp__github__list_issues` and `mcp__github__issue_read` return issue timestamps as `created_at`/`updated_at` (snake_case), while every downstream consumer of the fetched issue list — `parseRecordFacets` and `next`-ranking's oldest-first tie-break among them — reads camelCase `createdAt`/`updatedAt`. Observed live during a `/claude-tweaks:dispatch next` firing (run `2026-10-20T022848-record-3630`, 2026-10-20): the queue-pull had to patch `dispatch-groups.json` with camelCase aliases before ranking, or the oldest-first tie-break would silently degenerate to array order with no error surfaced.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Add a documented aliasing step to `mcp-transport.md`'s queue-pull section, naming the exact snake_case to camelCase fields a caller must alias before any ranking/eligibility computation.
- [ ] Prefer a code-level fix if cheap: alias the fields once, at the MCP-fetch boundary (whichever shared adapter normalizes an MCP-fetched issue into the shape `record.js`'s `parseRecordFacets` and `grouping.js` expect), so every MCP-path consumer gets the correct shape without each call site re-deriving the aliasing by hand.
- [ ] Add a conformance test or fixture pinning the expected camelCase shape for an MCP-sourced issue object.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `mcp-transport.md` names this gap and its required workaround, in the same style as its existing #3137/#2523/#1579 gap sections.
- A test (or documented manual check) confirms an MCP-fetched issue's `createdAt`/`updatedAt` resolve correctly for `next`-ranking's oldest-first tie-break.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Dispatch's MCP transport path now gets a correct oldest-first ranking tie-break instead of a silent array-order fallback.

Origin: ledger resolve gate (wrap-up of #3290)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

#3290 shipped the staged-patch stacked check (`plugin/bin/lib/staged-patch/stack-check.js`, `plugin/bin/check-staged-stack.js`, the console wiring in `plugin/bin/console-resolve.js` and `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js`). Its whole-branch review passed and the build's final review ruled fifteen minor findings ok-to-defer. Together they span six or more files, so no single fix-now pass covers them. They fall in four groups. Robustness: `headerSources` scans the whole patch including the free-text preamble, so a `rename from ../x` preamble line skips the patch and CRLF leaves `\r` in the source name; `isUnsafe` splits on `/` only; `rederive` gives the generic 'not a file in the worktree' reason for a file an earlier patch created; `git merge-file` exit 255 (a git error) is reported as 'conflict in {path}'; the STAGED conflict line names only the first conflict that involves the target. Portability: `defaultGit`'s `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devNull` is unverified on a Windows checkout and needs git 2.32 or newer. Coverage: no committed rename, new-file, deleted-file or binary patch case; untested `rederive` branches (already-satisfied, unsafe or not-in-patches guards, multi-file partial conflict, rename or delete refusal, numstat or summary failure) and untested CLI `rederiveReason` branches; the console's `checkPatchStack` wiring and its throw fail-closed branch have no test; the order-agreement test mirrors `readSnapshot`'s filter and sort instead of calling it; the `cli.test.js` shadow-refusal test asserts a vacuous `existsSync`. Contract pins and docs: `tests/staged-patch-contract.test.js` pins token presence only, not the re-run-once bound or the re-anchor condition, and its go-red control trips only the heading assertion; the `docs/plugin-structure.md` CLI line does not say exit 2 still prints the JSON line. Each item's detail and trigger is in the #3290 run ledger, `docs/plans/2026-10-19-staged-patch-stacked-check-ledger.md`, rows 1-15.

## Deliverables

Scan `headerSources` from the first `diff --git` line only and strip a trailing `\r` from a source name

Make `isUnsafe` reject a `..` segment split on `\` as well as `/`

Give `rederive` a specific refusal reason when the target file is created by an earlier staged patch

Report a `git merge-file` exit above 1 as a git error, not as 'conflict in {path}'

Name every conflict that involves the target in the stacked-check STAGED line, not only the first

Verify `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devNull` on a Windows runner and document or replace the git 2.32 requirement

Add committed `stack-check` cases for rename, new-file, deleted-file and binary patches

Add `rederive` branch tests: already-satisfied, unsafe path, target not in patches, multi-file partial conflict, rename or delete refusal, numstat or summary failure; make the same-anchor rederive test assert the reason, not only `/conflict/`

Add CLI tests for the `rederiveReason` branches: rederive refusal, rederive throw, `--rederive-out` with a non-conflicting target, `conflictsWith` equal to the target

Replace the vacuous shadow-refusal assertion in `tests/bin-lib/staged-patch/cli.test.js` with one that fails when the shadow is written

Test `plugin/bin/console-resolve.js`'s `checkPatchStack` wiring and its throw fail-closed branch

Make the stack-check order-agreement test call `readSnapshot` instead of mirroring its filter and sort

Make `tests/staged-patch-contract.test.js` go red on each assertion it claims, and pin the re-run-once bound and the re-anchor condition

State in `docs/plugin-structure.md` that exit 2 for an unapplicable target still prints the JSON line

## Acceptance Criteria

Each deliverable has a committed test or a changed assertion that fails when its fix is reverted

`npm test` passes with no new skips

The #3290 ledger rows 1-15 each name the commit or test that closes them

## Release Note

No user-visible change.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/staged-patch/stack-check.js` — robustness fixes
- `plugin/bin/check-staged-stack.js` — STAGED conflict line and exit-2 doc
- `tests/bin-lib/staged-patch/stack-check.test.js` — rename, new, delete, binary and rederive branch cases
- `tests/bin-lib/staged-patch/cli.test.js` — rederiveReason branches, shadow-refusal assertion
- `tests/staged-patch-contract.test.js` — go-red controls and pins
- `docs/plugin-structure.md` — exit 2 wording

Origin: ledger resolve gate

Defer-reason: tangential

**Related:** #3674

## Current State

The flaky-retry hook substitutes each failing file path into the suite's `retry` template with `template.replace(/\{file\}/g, file)` (`plugin/bin/lib/verify/flaky.js`) and runs it under `{ shell: true }` (`plugin/bin/lib/verify/run.js`). The path comes from the runner's own output and is filtered only by `TEST_FILE_RE`, a suffix check (`plugin/bin/lib/verify/extract.js`), so a name carrying shell metacharacters passes. This predates #3480 for the spec and TAP families, which #3480 extended to the jest/vitest summary family. A real, benign form: vitest's multi-project prefix prints `FAIL  |unit| tests/a.test.ts`, which the extractor captures as the file `|unit| tests/a.test.ts`; the substituted command becomes a pipeline that exits 127, so the retry fails safe rather than clearing anything. Found by the #3480 review lens 3b (single agent, low confidence).

## Deliverables

- [ ] Quote the substituted `{file}` (or run the retry template without a shell) so a path cannot add shell syntax.

- [ ] Strip a vitest `|project|` prefix from the captured summary-family path, or refuse a path containing whitespace or shell metacharacters with a named `retryDecision.reason`.

- [ ] Tests: a path with `$(…)` and a `|unit|` prefixed vitest log, each asserting the command run and the decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A failing file whose printed path contains shell metacharacters never reaches the shell as syntax.

- [ ] A vitest multi-project log retries the real test file, or refuses with a named reason.

- [ ] Each new test goes red when its fix is reverted.

## Release Note

Runner-owned flaky retry no longer passes an unquoted, runner-printed file path to the shell.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/flaky.js` — modify
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/extract.js` — modify

Origin: #3562 Deliverable 4 (run 2026-10-19T212245-record-3562) — sibling files with the same CRLF read-plus-extract shape, kept out of #3562 by its own Gotchas

Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

## Current State

#3562 fixed `tests/pipeline-run-dir-adoption-anchoring.test.js` for Windows checkouts: it read live skill markdown with a raw `fs.readFileSync(…, 'utf8')` and applied a bare-`\n` fence regex, which matches nothing once `core.autocrlf=true` gives the doc `\r\n` endings. Its sibling grep (`git grep -lE '```(bash|sh|js|json|yaml|yml)?\\n' -- tests tools`), re-run on this record's build branch (base `4dbf60b8d`), finds ten more files with the same read-plus-extract shape that no open record claims (an open-issue search for each filename returns only #3562 itself, which names them as out of scope). Each reads governed markdown raw and extracts with a bare-`\n` anchored regex:

| File | Raw read | Extractor |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/bin-lib/issues/labels.test.js` | line 126 | line 127, `## Canonical LABELS_JSON[\s\S]*?```js\n([\s\S]*?)\n```` |
| `tests/blast-radius-snippet.test.js` | line 17 | line 18, `is one CLI call[^\n]*\n[^\n]*\n\n```bash\n([^`]+)```` |
| `tests/capture-native-branch-guard-shapes.test.js` | line 28 | line 25, ````bash\n([\s\S]*?)```` |
| `tests/harness-health-runaway-section.test.js` | line 13 | line 27, ````bash\n\s*node -e '…' ` |
| `tests/init-port-isolation-conformance.test.js` | line 13 | line 90, an exact fenced `ports.js allocate` line |
| `tests/plan-audit-check-e-prose.test.js` | line 17 | line 72, `## Invocation\s+```bash\n([^\n]+)\n```` |
| `tests/tidy-release-note-repair-conformance.test.js` | line 10 | line 81, then runs it with `bash -c` (lines 85-86) |
| `tests/dispatch-firing-exclusion.test.js` | line 24 | line 30, then runs it with `bash -c` (line 58) |
| `tests/multispec-not-run-callsite.test.js` | line 22 | line 46, then runs it with `bash -c` (line 96) |
| `tests/verify-expectations-writer-conformance.test.js` | line 16 | line 54, then runs it with `execFileSync('/bin/sh', …)` (line 66) |

Per #3562's Current State, all ten fail on `windows-latest` with an extractor-not-found message. Four of them also run what they extract, so a second Windows layer can sit behind the CRLF one, as #3517, #3555, #3565 and #3587 found: `\r` left in a captured snippet breaks `bash -c`; a native backslash `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` interpolated into a heredoc turns into JS escapes; and a literal `/bin/sh` resolves to `<drive>:\bin\sh` on win32 and throws `ENOENT`. #3565's sweep records `verify-expectations-writer-conformance.test.js:66`'s `/bin/sh` spawn as masked behind the CRLF extraction failure, with no open record owning it.

## Deliverables

1. For each of the ten files above, read the governed markdown through `tests/helpers/read-skill.js`'s `readText()` instead of a raw `fs.readFileSync`. Leave every extraction regex as it is — `readText()` normalizes at the read, so an extracted snippet is LF and runnable on every checkout.
2. For each file that runs what it extracts (`tidy-release-note-repair-conformance`, `dispatch-firing-exclusion`, `multispec-not-run-callsite`, `verify-expectations-writer-conformance`), check the second layer and fix it test-side: a forward-slash `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` where one is interpolated into a script, and no literal `/bin/sh` spawn target (`verify-expectations-writer-conformance.test.js:66` — use `bash` from the inherited `PATH`, as the sibling `bash -c` suites that pass on `windows-latest` do).
3. Add one CRLF control per extractor, built from the LF `readText()` value with `.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n')` (assert `\r\n` present and no `\r\r\n`), proving the read-plus-extract path returns the same result as for the LF text — the pattern #3562 added to `tests/pipeline-run-dir-adoption-anchoring.test.js`.
4. Before opening the PR, re-run the sibling grep above and re-check open records; drop any file another record claims by then and record the grep output in the PR body.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of the ten files passes `node --test` on macOS/Linux with no test removed, skipped or weakened, plus its new CRLF control.
- [ ] CRLF simulation on macOS/Linux: a scratch copy of `tests/` and `plugin/` with the governed docs converted to `\r\n` fails the pre-fix files with their extractor messages and passes the fixed files. Quote both runs' `# pass` / `# fail` lines in the PR body.
- [ ] All ten files pass on `windows-latest`. Prove it before merge by dispatching `gh workflow run windows-regression.yml --ref {branch}` and quoting each file's per-test `ok` lines from the run's log, not the adjudication verdict alone (a dispatch baselines against `HEAD^1`, #3568). If the dispatch cannot run, say so explicitly.
- [ ] Each new CRLF control discriminates: replacing its `readText(` with a raw `fs.readFileSync(…, 'utf8')` turns it red. Run each doctoring in the same command as its restore.
- [ ] No file under `plugin/` changes.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fixed ten skill-prose tests that failed only on Windows checkouts because of line endings.

## Technical Approach

Test-side only, following `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md`'s "Build CRLF inputs from the LF text" pattern and its Anti-Patterns row "Treating a CRLF fix as the whole Windows fix for a test that extracts and runs a skill's shell snippet". `readText()` is the repo's single EOL-normalizing read for governed markdown; `skill-prose-conformance-tests` already requires it for every prose suite. Normalize at the read, not with a `\r?\n`-tolerant regex: a suite that runs its extracted snippet would still hand `bash -c` a snippet full of `\r` (reproduced in #3562's scratch run).

- `tests/bin-lib/issues/labels.test.js`, `tests/blast-radius-snippet.test.js`, `tests/capture-native-branch-guard-shapes.test.js`, `tests/harness-health-runaway-section.test.js`, `tests/init-port-isolation-conformance.test.js`, `tests/plan-audit-check-e-prose.test.js` — read-only extract-and-compare suites: route the read through `readText()`, add a CRLF control

- `tests/helpers/read-skill.js` — read-only reference: `readText()`
- `tests/pipeline-run-dir-adoption-anchoring.test.js` — read-only reference: #3562's CRLF control shape
- `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md` — read-only reference

## Gotchas

- Do not add a `.gitattributes` `eol=lf` rule for `tests/` or the skill files; the parity skill scopes it to the hashed upstream-drift fixtures on purpose.
- Do not build a CRLF case from a raw read: on a Windows checkout that yields `\r\r\n` (#3523). Build it from the `readText()` value.
- The second-layer failures are inferred for most files, not observed: the CRLF extractor failure masks them on Windows today. Investigate whatever shape the dispatched Windows run shows; never add a win32 skip to turn a run green.
- If this proves too large for one PR, split it along the read-only / extract-and-run line — the four extract-and-run files each need their own Windows proof.

## Current State

`plugin/bin/wrap-up-engine.js` `plan` resolves its fact-gathering root with `resolveRepoRoot(process.cwd())`, which returns the directory above `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`. From a linked worktree that is the MAIN checkout, not the worktree. The root was written for telemetry (anchor to the main checkout), and #3017 reused it for `gatherFacts({ cwd, base })` as well, so `plan` run from a worktree computes `git diff --name-only {base}...HEAD`, the renamed/deleted list, the journey `files:` overlap, and the `docs/`/`CLAUDE.md` filesystem facts against the main checkout's HEAD and tree.

Observed on #3598 (run 2026-10-19T201721-record-3598): `plan` run from the dispatch worktree listed two renames of archived run-dir spec files (3571, 3573) as the `references` row candidates and returned an empty journeys overlap list, although the branch diff held only added and modified files and one journey it had edited. `plugin/bin/friction-events.js` returns `[]` for a run that logged real friction, whenever the operator's timezone is ahead of UTC. `computeClaimBoundary(runDir)` reads the first `decisions.md` entry's `HH:MM:SS` and builds a `Date` from the string `{mintDay}T{HH:MM:SS}Z`, i.e. it parses that time as UTC. `plugin/bin/lib/log-decision/append.js` writes it with `getHours()/getMinutes()/getSeconds()`, i.e. in local time. `events.jsonl` timestamps are UTC (`toISOString`). On a CEST host the claim line `20:59:10` becomes `20:59:10Z`, two hours after the real claim (`18:59:10Z`), so every event the run logged before then is dropped as "pre-claim noise" (#2989).

Observed in the #3498 run (2026-10-19, CEST): `events.jsonl` held 12 `wd-guard-refusal` events (11 of them after the real claim), and `node plugin/bin/friction-events.js --run <run-dir>` printed `[]`. `/claude-tweaks:reflect`'s Friction lens treats `[]` as "consistent with a frictionless run", so the lens had no evidence to judge. The mirror case (a host behind UTC) lets pre-claim noise through instead, which is the failure #2989 fixed.

- [ ] Make `computeClaimBoundary` interpret `decisions.md`'s clock time in the same zone `log-decision/append.js` wrote it in, or have `append.js` persist an unambiguous instant the reader can parse without guessing (expand-contract: keep reading the existing `HH:MM:SS` form for runs already on disk).

`reconcile --checks` runs exactly the named subset, but `archive` silently depends on `mirror`: `archive-merged.js`'s `localHasMerge` needs the integration branch's merge commit to be an ancestor of `refs/heads/{integration}` or `origin/{integration}`, and only `mirror` (or `remote-prune`) runs the fetch that makes `origin/{integration}` current. A caller who names `archive` without `mirror` gets a silent `local-behind-merge` skip for any PR GitHub merged asynchronously.

Nothing in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/index.js` or `docs/reconcile-checks.md` declares this prerequisite. #3026's drain-termination call was specified as `--checks release,archive,reap`, which would have shipped the defect; it was caught only by the final whole-branch review and corrected to `mirror,release,archive,reap`. The only other scripted subset caller, `_shared/pr-first-merge-post-merge.md` Step 4.2, names `mirror` by hand.

## Deliverables

1. `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/index.js` declares each check's prerequisite checks (`archive` needs `mirror`, and any other dependency the code shows) and expands an explicit `checks` subset with them before dispatch, preserving the existing dispatch order.

2. `docs/reconcile-checks.md` documents the prerequisite table and that an explicit subset is expanded and runs without the hot-path time ceiling.

3. `tests/reconcile.test.js` pins the expansion: a `checks: ['archive']` request runs `mirror` first; an unrelated subset is not widened.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Current State

`.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md` is the project skill for Windows test-parity fixes. Its Anti-Patterns table does not yet cover four patterns that the Windows records #3440, #3505 and #3506 hit, and that the next `windows-regression` filing will hit again:

- a fixture home passed to a spawned child through `HOME` alone (`os.homedir()` reads `USERPROFILE` on win32),
- a `#!/bin/sh` script named `gh` put on `PATH` to fake the CLI (`execFileSync('gh')` never spawns it on win32),
- a POSIX `'/tmp'` literal used as a spawn `cwd` or `repoRoot`,
- fixing only the assertions a failure excerpt or spec names (the first `windows-latest` run on #3505's branch still failed two sibling assertions in the same file).

The wrap-up Skills row drafted these rows during the run for #3440, #3505 and #3506 and then withdrew them from that PR: an agent-instruction edit fails `merge-check`'s refutation test, and it would have parked three one-file test fixes for a human. The drafted rows are in the Deliverables below. Open PRs #3569 and #3540 also append rows to the same table, so expect to merge by hand; place the new rows mid-table (after the `Mapping every spawn throw…` row) to avoid an adjacent-hunk conflict.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Add the four rows below to the Anti-Patterns table of `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md`, after the `Mapping every spawn throw to a "not installed" or "not found" verdict` row, keeping each claim accurate against the files it cites (re-check the line references first).
- [ ] If #3540 has not merged its `chmod 0o000` row by then, check whether the skill still lacks one and say so in the PR; do not duplicate it.

  | Pointing a spawned child at a fixture home with `HOME` alone (`env: { ...process.env, HOME: home }`) | `os.homedir()` reads `USERPROFILE` on win32, so the child searches the runner's real profile and every transcript lookup reports "not found". Set both keys to the fixture home, and drop an inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` so a developer's own config dir cannot redirect the lookup: `tests/bin-lib/timing/cli.test.js`'s `fixtureHomeEnv` (#3440; `tests/statusline.test.js` records the same behavior) |
  | A test that puts a `#!/bin/sh` script named `gh` on `PATH` to fake the CLI | `execFileSync('gh')` never spawns an extensionless script on win32, so the test fails there for a reason that has nothing to do with the code under test. Skip every test that writes such a stub with one per-file constant that states the reason (`PATH_STUB_SKIP` in `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/pr-state.test.js` and `release-merged.test.js`, #3506), and leave the tests that remove `gh` from `PATH` running: they pass on Windows. Judge each test by whether it writes a stub, not by its title |
  | Passing a POSIX literal such as `'/tmp'` as a spawn `cwd` or `repoRoot` | The directory does not exist on Windows, so the spawn fails with `ENOENT` and reads as a missing binary. Take a real directory from the OS: `os.tmpdir()` (#3506). A deliberately nonexistent path stays literal when the test is about that case |
  | Fixing only the assertions a failure excerpt or a spec names | The filer's excerpt shows the first failing tests, and a spec written from it can miss siblings with the same shape. #3505's spec listed five `${dir}/…` lines in `tests/bin-lib/console/residue.test.js`; the first `windows-latest` run on the branch still failed two more in that file (`(spec-12/console.json)` and `(spec-2/console.json)`, built with `path.relative`). Grep the whole file for the separator literal, and read the per-file isolated log of a dispatched `windows-regression.yml` run on the branch before calling the fix done |

**Related:** #3079, #3284, #3289, #3295, #3297, #3363, #3377, #3378, #3442, #3483, #3496, #3503, #3510, #3515, #3577

## Current State

Spec #3520's Deliverable 5 told `/dispatch` to log a decision line with the word `STAGED`. That line was copied from a warning #1985 had already added to `plugin/skills/dispatch/drain-pr-overlap.md`. Neither line writes a `staged/` artifact, so both violated the Status semantics in `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-decision-log.md:139-156`, where `STAGED` requires a proposal written to the run's `staged/` directory and `STAGED`/`SKIP` are disjoint by the presence of a staged artifact. An informational "dispatched anyway" warning is `AUTO`.

The SDD final whole-branch review flagged it as Minor 4. The controller ruled to keep the line because the spec mandated that exact text. Review lens 3a then reproduced the finding, and commit `ccca47271` on PR #3530 changed all three lines to `AUTO`. That cost #3520 one wrong ruling and one review-fix commit.

Two gaps let it through, and both were verified on the current tree:

- `/claude-tweaks:specify` has no check that a literal `decisions.md` line mandated by a spec uses a status word consistent with `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`'s Status semantics. Its two composition paths, `plugin/skills/specify/shaping-mode.md` (shaping) and `plugin/skills/specify/record-creation-subissues.md` (decomposition), carry no such check today.
- `/claude-tweaks:build`'s SDD invocation instruction (`plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md`) never says that a project contract outranks spec-mandated literal text. A ruling can therefore keep a contract violation because the spec spelled it out.

## Deliverables

1. `/claude-tweaks:specify`: when a composed spec mandates a literal `decisions.md` line, check its status word against `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`'s Status semantics before the record is written or stamped `ready`. A `STAGED` line must name the `staged/` artifact it writes. A line that writes no artifact must use `AUTO`, or `SKIP` for a degrade trace. Add this check in both composition paths: shaping (`shaping-mode.md`) and decomposition (`record-creation-subissues.md`). On a mismatch, rewrite the line to the contract-conformant status before writing; never stop mid-flow to ask.
2. `/claude-tweaks:build`: in `plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md`'s SDD invocation instruction, state that spec-mandated literal text does not override a project contract (`_shared/*.md`). When the two conflict, the ruling conforms to the contract and records the change as an update-the-spec deviation (`build-deviation-*`). The spec's text is never kept on the grounds that the spec spelled it out.
3. Two conformance tests, one per instruction, each pinning the instruction's presence in its file.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A conformance test fails when the literal-decision-line status-word check is removed from `plugin/skills/specify/shaping-mode.md` or from `plugin/skills/specify/record-creation-subissues.md`.
2. A conformance test fails when the "contract beats spec-mandated literal text" instruction is removed from `plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md`.
3. Neither change adds a new mid-flow stop in `auto` mode. The specify check rewrites rather than prompts, and the build instruction directs a ruling rather than a question.
4. Both new tests pass on the changed tree, and each fails when its instruction is reverted (proved by temporarily reverting the instruction).

## Release Note

Spec shaping now corrects a mandated decision-log line whose status word breaks the decision-log contract, and builds now side with the project contract over conflicting spec wording.

## Technical Approach

- Add the specify check next to each composition path's existing premise-verification step (`shaping-mode.md`'s premise-verification paragraph; `record-creation-subissues.md`'s Premise verification paragraph). Cite `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`'s Status semantics rather than restating the vocabulary.
- Add the build instruction to `build/dispatch.md`'s SDD invocation instruction, beside the existing ruling-related directives (the SDD `Ruling:` carry-forward paragraph). Reuse the existing `build-deviation-*` staged-item convention.
- The tests follow the existing prose-conformance pattern (`tests/build-*.test.js`, `tests/specify-*.test.js`), reading the live skill text.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/specify/shaping-mode.md`: add the literal-decision-line status-word check (shaping path)
- `plugin/skills/specify/record-creation-subissues.md`: add the same check (decomposition path)
- `plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md`: add the "contract beats spec-mandated literal text" ruling instruction to the SDD invocation
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-decision-log.md`: read only; its Status semantics section is the cited contract
- `tests/specify-decision-line-status-word.test.js`: new conformance test for Deliverable 1
- `tests/build-contract-beats-spec-literal.test.js`: new conformance test for Deliverable 2

## Gotchas

- Byte-pinned prose tests elsewhere may cover the paragraphs being edited in `build/dispatch.md` and `shaping-mode.md`. Run the full suite, not only the new tests (`npm test`).
- `build/dispatch.md`'s SDD invocation paragraph is a single very long line. Insert the new sentence without reflowing the surrounding text, so unrelated byte pins don't break.

## Original request

## Current State

Spec #3520's Deliverable 5 told `/dispatch` to log a decision line with the word `STAGED`. It copied that line from the warning #1985 had already added to `plugin/skills/dispatch/drain-pr-overlap.md`. Neither line writes a `staged/` artifact, so both broke the Status semantics in `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-decision-log.md`: `STAGED` requires a staged file, and an informational "dispatched anyway" warning should be `AUTO`.

The SDD final whole-branch review flagged the problem as Minor 4. The controller ruled to keep the line because the spec required that exact text. Review lens 3a then reproduced the finding, and commit ccca472 on PR #3530 changed all three lines to `AUTO`. Two gaps let this happen:

# Reflect — staged finding 1

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect hindsight from #3401

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md` line 14 carries two "append a ledger row, then stage a file, then log STAGED" procedures that an LLM controller performs by hand: the `build-deviation-{N}` staging and, since #3401, the SDD `Ruling:` carry-forward. Each is a three-step prose dance whose coupling is the ledger item number the staged file's `Ledger:` header must name — so the row is appended first, the file second, and the row's Item text is rewritten afterwards when `stage-item.js --allocate` renumbers the id.

#3401's own review found five failure-branch gaps in that prose in a single pass (run ledger `docs/plans/2026-10-17-sdd-ruling-console-ledger.md` rows 20-24: no `stage-item.js` failure branch, an unsanctioned Item-cell rewrite, De-duplication on Append swallowing a second ruling, a reverse write-back ordered before the record number existed, an empty-resolution path `finish-console` rejects). Every one of them is a step a mechanical writer would not have been able to skip. Refs #3401.

## Deliverables

A `--ledger <path>` mode on `plugin/bin/stage-item.js` (or a sibling `bin/carry-forward.js`) that, in one call: appends the ledger row through `bin/lib/wrap-up/ledger-write.js`'s table parser (never De-duplication on Append), allocates the staged id, writes the staged file with `Ledger: {path}#{item}` already filled, prints the actual path, and logs the `STAGED` line via `bin/lib/log-decision/append.js`'s `formatEntry`; on any failure after the append it strips the `(staged/…)` suffix from the row it wrote and logs the Degrade-trace `SKIP` line itself.

`dispatch.md`'s `build-deviation-{N}` and `sdd-ruling-{N}` prose each collapse to one CLI invocation plus the one-liner they pass; the hand-performed ordering, renumbering, failure, and dedupe clauses added by #3401 and its review are deleted, not kept beside the CLI.

Conformance pins in `tests/build-sdd-ledger-residue-carryforward.test.js` and the build-deviation suite point at the CLI call; a CLI test proves the failure branch leaves the row `open` without a staged suffix.

## Acceptance Criteria

`grep -c "stage-item.js" plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md` prints at least `2` and `grep -c "update the just-appended row" plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md` prints `0`.

A CLI test appends a ruling row to a fixture ledger, stages `sdd-ruling-1.md`, and asserts the staged file's `Ledger:` header names the appended item number and the row's Item cell names the path the CLI actually wrote; a second test forces the write to fail and asserts the row is `open` with no `(staged/` substring and a `SKIP … (degraded): condition:` line was logged.

`npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Build: SDD ruling and build-deviation carry-forwards now stage through one CLI call, so a failed staging can no longer leave a ledger row pointing at a file that was never written.

Origin: #3310 whole-branch review (final review Minor 5)

Defer-reason: out-of-scope

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/checks.js`'s `headroomCheck` measures each governed `.md` file with the raw `fs.statSync(abs).size`, which counts `when:` marker lines and CRLF line endings. Since #3310 it compares that raw figure to `RAIL_BYTES` (52,500 B).

The Read rail measures differently. `rail.js`'s `skillFileRailViolations` goes through `context-cost.js`'s `measureSkills`/`measureSubFiles`, which strip marker lines and normalize CRLF to LF. `plugin/skills/build/plan-audit.md` now says the rail strips only the marker lines.

Raw bytes are always greater than or equal to measured bytes, so plan-audit never misses a breach. The cost is a false positive: a marker-heavy file, or any file in a Windows CRLF checkout, sitting slightly over `RAIL_BYTES` raw gets a blocking plan-audit stop that the `rail:` tests would pass. The raw basis predates #3310; #3310 only retargeted the number.

## Deliverables

- `headroomCheck` measures per-file bytes through `context-cost.js`'s marker-stripped, CRLF-normalized measurement, the same function the rail uses. It reuses that function rather than re-implementing the stripping.
- `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/checks.test.js` gains a fixture that is over `RAIL_BYTES` raw but under it once marker lines are stripped. That fixture reports no breach. A CRLF variant does the same.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A governed fixture file whose raw size is `RAIL_BYTES + 100`, carrying more than 100 B of `<!-- when: … -->` marker lines, reports no `breaches` entry.
2. The same file with its marker lines removed, and its body padded so it stays over `RAIL_BYTES`, still reports a breach.
3. A CRLF copy of a file at exactly `RAIL_BYTES` LF bytes reports no breach.
4. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Plan audits measure a skill file's size the same way the Read-limit check does, so marker lines and Windows line endings no longer trigger a false stop.

## Current State

During #3249's review (14 lens agents, 7 reproduction pairs at `review-effort: high`), lens 3a's (Convention) reproduction pair disagreed: one agent (3a-A) returned no findings; the other (3a-B) returned `STATUS: BLOCKED`, citing several specific functions, exports, and parameters as "completely missing from the codebase" — with exact line-number citations drawn from the record's own materialized plan file (which shows the code to add). Every one of those claims was false: direct `grep` against the live worktree confirmed every named item already existed exactly as claimed-missing (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js:242,326`; `release-merged.js:16,360,365,385`; `archive-merged.js:320`). The agent appears to have conflated the plan document's own illustrative "add this code" listing with the code's current applied state.

The reproduction-pair mechanism (`plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md`) correctly flagged this as a disagreement, but its own handling treats *any* disagreement as `unconfirmed`/low-confidence, which is the right default for a genuine judgment call but is not the cheapest-available resolution for this specific claim shape: "a named function/export/parameter does not exist" is mechanically, cheaply verifiable (one `grep`/`Read`) before ever reaching a human at the Review Console. Without an explicit instruction to do that check, a differently-briefed session could plausibly have accepted the disagreement as "needs a human to judge" and left a factually-false BLOCKED claim staged as merely low-confidence, sending a human to investigate a non-existent gap.

## Deliverables

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A reproduction-pair disagreement where one side asserts code/export/parameter absence that a one-command `grep`/`Read` check can mechanically refute no longer reaches the Wrap-Up Review Console as a merely low-confidence item — it resolves to refuted before routing.

Review's reproduction-pair handling gains a cheap ground-truth check for mechanically-falsifiable "code is missing" disagreements, reducing false BLOCKED verdicts reaching the Review Console.

## Current State

`cmdStop` in `plugin/bin/lib/visual-decide/cli.js` sends `SIGTERM`, then `waitFor`s until either the `server-stopped` marker exists or `!pidAlive(info.pid)`. It writes the marker itself (`writeStoppedMarker`) only when `waitFor` times out, which is the zombie-PID case #3130 fixed.

On win32, `process.kill(pid, 'SIGTERM')` terminates the daemon unconditionally and its `SIGTERM` handler (`process.on('SIGTERM', stop)`, which writes `server-stopped`) never runs. `waitFor` then settles through `!pidAlive`, `settled` is true, and no marker is written. After a clean `stop`, `status` can then report the server as crashed rather than stopped. The same holds anywhere the PID dies without running its handler, such as SIGKILL by an outside actor between the signal and the poll.

The stuck-PID test in `tests/bin-lib/visual-decide/cli.test.js` is skipped on win32, and CI is ubuntu-only, so nothing exercises this path today. Reasoning from documented Node behavior; not observed on a Windows run.

## Deliverables

- In `cmdStop`, write the `server-stopped` marker whenever the wait settles without the marker present (PID gone or timeout), not only on timeout, so `stop` always leaves the marker behind.

- Add a platform-independent test: simulate a daemon whose PID disappears without writing the marker, and assert `stop` leaves `server-stopped` in place and `status` reports stopped.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/visual-decide/cli.js` — `cmdStop` marker write
- `tests/bin-lib/visual-decide/cli.test.js` — handler-less exit case

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After `stop` against a daemon that exits without running its SIGTERM handler, `server-stopped` exists and `status` reports stopped, not crashed.

- [ ] The new test runs on Linux CI and fails on the pre-fix `cmdStop`.

- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fix visual-decide `stop` sometimes leaving a cleanly stopped server reported as crashed on Windows.

## Current State

Claude Code 2.1.283+ ships a built-in `/prompt-audit` command. It reads CLAUDE.md files, skills, agents, and custom commands, and flags instructions written for older models, stale paths, and contradictory rules (source in the original request below).

What claude-tweaks already has in this space:

- `/claude-tweaks:harness-health` (`plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md`) audits `.claude/skills/*.md`, `.claude/rules/*.md` and CLAUDE.md against the codebase, a template, and best practice, one target per firing. It then files `by:harness-health` issues. Its stated scope is the project's own `.claude/` tree (this repo has 17 files under `.claude/skills/`), not the 39 shipped `plugin/skills/*/SKILL.md` files. Its target discovery reads only `<root>/.claude/skills` (`plugin/bin/lib/harness-health/scope.js:198`).
- `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s "Model-version prompting notes" section (line 215) is a manual checklist to re-run whenever a new Claude model ships. It covers model-version deltas and a verification/self-check instruction audit against `docs/reference/claude-quality-levers.md`. That is the "instructions written for older models" concern, done by hand.

So the open question has two parts: what `/prompt-audit` catches that neither harness-health nor the manual model-version checklist catches, and whether it reaches the shipped `plugin/skills/` library at all.

## Deliverables

1. Run `/prompt-audit` once against this repo's CLAUDE.md, `.claude/skills/`, `plugin/skills/`, and `plugin/agents/`, and keep its raw output.
2. A comparison, posted as a comment on this record, that sorts each finding into one of three buckets:
   - already covered by harness-health (name the harness-health check);
   - already covered by the model-version prompting checklist in `docs/skill-authoring.md`;
   - genuinely new.
3. For each genuinely new finding, take exactly one of two routes:
   - a backlog record via `/claude-tweaks:capture` with a spec-shaped body, either fixing the flagged instruction or extending harness-health or the checklist to catch that class;
   - a stated reason, in the comment, why it is not worth acting on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `/prompt-audit` has been run once over the targets in Deliverable 1. The comment states the Claude Code version used and the target set actually covered.
- Every finding in the run's output appears in the comparison comment under exactly one of the three buckets.
- Every genuinely new finding has either a linked filed backlog record or a stated reason for no action; none is left unrouted.
- The comment states whether `/prompt-audit` reached the `plugin/skills/` library, since harness-health does not.

## Release Note

No user-facing change. This produces an internal comparison of Claude Code's `/prompt-audit` against claude-tweaks' own harness-health audit.

## Technical Approach

Run `/prompt-audit` from an interactive session at the repo root. Then work through its findings against two references: harness-health's analysis criteria (`plugin/skills/_shared/harness-health-analysis.md`, the shared judge procedure) and the model-version checklist. Fixes to individual skills are not made in this record; they are filed as follow-ups so each lands with its own conformance-test run.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/harness-health/SKILL.md` — the existing audit whose coverage is compared
- `plugin/skills/_shared/harness-health-analysis.md` — harness-health's shared judge procedure
- `docs/skill-authoring.md` — the manual model-version prompting checklist (line 215)
- `docs/reference/claude-quality-levers.md` — the levers that checklist audits against

## Gotchas

- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: `/prompt-audit` can be run on demand in this environment and accepts the `plugin/` subtree as a target. It is a built-in slash command, so a headless agent may not be able to invoke it the same way. Confirm before relying on an unattended run.
- Fixing a flagged skill instruction here would touch shipped prose that conformance tests pin repo-wide (`tests/` byte-pins skill text). That is why fixes go to follow-up records, each with its own full-suite run.
- harness-health's own scope is `.claude/` by design. A finding that it misses on `plugin/skills/` is a scope question, not automatically a harness-health defect.

Run /prompt-audit against claude-tweaks' own CLAUDE.md and skills

Current State:
- Claude Code's /prompt-audit (v2.1.283+) reads CLAUDE.md files, skills, agents, and custom commands, flagging instructions written for older models, stale paths, and contradictory rules.
- claude-tweaks ships a large skill library that has not been audited against the new Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 models this way.

Deliverables:

Acceptance Criteria:
- /prompt-audit run once with findings reviewed.
- Any genuinely new findings (not already covered by harness-health) turned into follow-up fixes or a harness-health improvement.

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3047

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:test`'s pipeline path with `VERIFICATION_PASSED=true` and stories present (`plugin/skills/test/SKILL.md:70`) selects QA stories by `source_files` ∩ `node bin/verify.js --changed-files --integration-branch {ref}`. `--changed-files` (`plugin/bin/verify.js:156`, `changedFilesMode`) resolves its base through `resolveBase` (`plugin/bin/lib/verify/changed-files.js:54`) with this precedence: `--base` first, then the checkout's own verification-stamp anchor whenever it is usable and not equal to HEAD (`:62-77`), and only then the `--integration-branch` merge-base (`:78-84`).

In a `/flow` run, `/build` Common Step 5 writes the stamp. Bookkeeping commits follow (for example `/stories` committing a new story YAML), so by the time `/test` selects stories the stamp anchor is an ancestor of HEAD but not HEAD. The changed-file set is then only the post-stamp bookkeeping, never the build's own source changes. Observed (reporter, plugin 6.136.0): the set was a single `stories/*.yaml` file. No story's `source_files` matched it, the Layer-3 UI sniff found no UI trigger file in it, and the documented path would have reported `QA: skipped — no affected stories` for a build that had just changed three admin-UI components. The reporter selected stories by hand against `git diff --name-only <merge-base>..HEAD`.

The stamp anchor is the right base for re-running tests (`affected`, `verification.md`'s Re-verify scoping table): the stamp records what was already verified. It is the wrong base for QA story selection, because the stamp says nothing about QA. `plugin/skills/test/design-gate.md:9` reads the same `--changed-files` set to decide which files the design CLI gate judges, so it has the same blind spot.

## Deliverables

1. Add an opt-in `--ignore-stamp` flag to `verify.js --changed-files` (parsed in `plugin/bin/lib/verify/args.js`, honored by `changedFilesMode`/`resolveBase`). It skips the stamp anchor and resolves the base from `--base` or the `--integration-branch` merge-base, keeping the existing exit-1 and `warning: resolved base equals HEAD` semantics. Reject it outside `--changed-files` the way the other read-only flags are rejected.
2. Switch `test/SKILL.md`'s pipeline QA story selection (`:70`) to `verify.js --changed-files --ignore-stamp --integration-branch {ref}`, so selection compares story `source_files` against the run's own branch diff.
3. Switch `test/design-gate.md:9`'s `<changed-files>` resolution to the same `--ignore-stamp` form.
4. Leave `/claude-tweaks:test affected` (test re-runs) and `verification.md`'s Re-verify scoping unchanged — they keep the stamp-anchored set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a stamp anchored at commit A, a later source commit B, and a bookkeeping commit C on HEAD, `verify.js --changed-files --integration-branch {ref}` still returns only C's files, and `--changed-files --ignore-stamp --integration-branch {ref}` returns B's and C's files (the merge-base diff). Both cases are covered in `tests/bin-lib/verify/changed-files.test.js` and/or `cli.test.js`.
- `--ignore-stamp` with no resolvable `--base`/`--integration-branch` base exits 1 with a message, never an empty list.
- `--ignore-stamp` combined with a non-`--changed-files` mode is a usage error (exit 2), covered by `args.test.js`.
- `test/SKILL.md`'s QA selection and `design-gate.md` both name the `--ignore-stamp` form; the `affected` mode does not.
- The existing `verify` suites (`node --test tests/bin-lib/verify/*.test.js`) pass.

## Release Note

Select pipeline QA stories against the run's full branch diff, so a build's own UI changes are never skipped because a verification stamp was written before them.

## Technical Approach

An additive flag keeps every existing `--changed-files` caller's behavior unchanged. Flipping the default would change the `affected`/`--scope` semantics that rely on the stamp anchor. The alternative of passing `--base $(git merge-base …)` from the skill prose was rejected: that hand-rolls merge-base resolution (`preferOriginRef`, degenerate-base handling) that `resolveBase` already owns.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/args.js` — parse and validate `--ignore-stamp`
- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — pass the flag through `changedFilesMode`
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/changed-files.js` — `resolveBase` skips the stamp anchor when asked
- `plugin/skills/test/SKILL.md` — QA story selection uses `--ignore-stamp`
- `plugin/skills/test/design-gate.md` — design-gate changed-file set uses `--ignore-stamp`
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/changed-files.test.js` — stamp-anchored vs ignore-stamp base cases
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/args.test.js` — flag validation

## Gotchas

- `verify.js`'s usage string (`args.js:14`) and `verification.md`'s `--changed-files` description must name the new flag. Grep for every `--changed-files` mention in `plugin/skills/` before finishing (`test/SKILL.md`, `test/design-gate.md`, `test/verification.md`).
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/snippet-conformance.test.js` does not currently pin the `--changed-files` snippet. Run the full `npm test` anyway, because other conformance suites pin `test/SKILL.md` prose repo-wide.
- The reporter's alternative base (the run's materialize commit's parent) was not chosen. The integration-branch merge-base is already resolvable by `verify.js` without run-dir knowledge, and on a pr-first branch it is the same diff.

## Original request

test: pipeline QA story selection reads only post-stamp changes, so it can skip the build's own UI change

**Component:** claude-tweaks `skills/test` (pipeline QA selection) + `bin/verify.js --changed-files`
**Kind:** gap

## What happened

Inside a `/flow` run, `/build` Common Step 5 writes the verification pass stamp. `/stories` then commits a new story YAML, and `/test` (with `VERIFICATION_PASSED=true` and stories present) selects stories by `source_files ∩ verify.js --changed-files`. Because `--changed-files` resolves its base to the stamp's `fullSha` whenever that sha is an ancestor of HEAD, the set at that point is only the post-stamp commits — here a single `stories/*.yaml` file. No story's `source_files` matched it, the Layer-3 UI sniff found no UI trigger file in that one-file set, and the documented path would have reported `QA: skipped — no affected stories` for a build that had just changed three admin-UI components.

## Expected

The pipeline's QA selection should compare story `source_files` against the run's own change set (the branch diff from its merge-base / the run's materialize base), not against "changes since the last verification stamp", which in a pipeline is almost always just the bookkeeping that follows `/build`.

## Workaround used

Selected stories manually against the branch diff (`git diff --name-only <merge-base>..HEAD`) and logged the deviation to `decisions.md`.

## Suggested fix

Give `/test`'s pipeline selection its own base (the run's materialize commit's parent, or `--integration-branch` merge-base) instead of the stamp-anchored `--changed-files`, or add a `--since-base` mode to `verify.js --changed-files` that ignores the stamp.

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2987

## Current State

`plugin/bin/verify.js` writes the pass stamp only for a passing run of the full resolved check set: the write gate requires `fullSet && !parsed.noStamp` (verify.js ~line 568). `plugin/skills/test/verification.md:48` requires any deliberately partial `--cmd` set to pass `--no-stamp`, because the runner cannot tell a partial set from the full one. Both rules are correct on their own.

Together they leave a long suite with no way to earn a stamp. A project whose declared checks take about 25 minutes end to end must split verification into chunks under the harness's 10-minute foreground Bash cap. Every chunk is partial, so every chunk passes `--no-stamp`, and `--stamp-status` never reads `verifiedHead: true`. Every later gate (`/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5, the second call of a dispatched two-call group, skip-if-recent) then re-runs the whole set, so the two-call dispatch form pays the full ~25 minutes twice even when HEAD did not move. Agent-written stamps are forbidden (#1921), correctly, so there is no workaround. Reported on plugin 6.136.0.

Why not a single background run: `plugin/skills/test/verification.md:46`'s Foreground rule already permits one full-set run with `run_in_background` when the set exceeds the 600 s foreground cap — but only for the orchestrating session. "A dispatched subagent never backgrounds it — its turn cannot wait on a notification" (the `[IL-108]` family; #1904 stalled waiting on a background verify child's notification that never arrived). `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s two-call form runs each `/flow` call as a dispatched subagent, so inside those calls the 600 s cap is hard and chunking is the only sanctioned option. That is the case this record targets.

## Deliverables

1. A per-suite stamp mode: `verify.js --stamp-suite` (or equivalent) records, for a passing chunk, which declared checks passed against which sha and tree state, written by the runner only.
2. `--stamp-status` composes `verifiedHead: true` when every check declared in `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` (types, lint, and each declared suite) has a passing per-suite record at the current clean HEAD.
3. A per-suite record never counts toward a different sha, a dirty tree, or a check it did not run; a failing chunk clears or never writes its record.
4. `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` documents the chunked flow: when to use it, and that `--no-stamp` stays required for ad hoc partial runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Running each declared check in separate `verify.js` invocations with the per-suite mode, all passing at one clean HEAD, makes `--stamp-status` report `verifiedHead: true`.
2. If any declared check has no passing record at the current HEAD, `verifiedHead` stays `false`.
3. A per-suite record from an earlier sha, or written against a dirty tree, does not count.
4. A plain `--no-stamp` partial run still writes nothing.
5. The verify stamp tests pass, with new cases for 1–4.

## Release Note

Long test suites can now be verified in chunks under the 10-minute command limit and still earn a full verification stamp.

## Technical Approach

Store per-suite pass records alongside the existing stamp (same git-dir location, runner-written), keyed by sha and check name. Have `--stamp-status` compute the full-coverage verdict from the declared check list in `verify-scope.json`. Keep the existing full-run stamp unchanged so current callers see no difference.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — new flag, write path, and `--stamp-status` composition

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3002

## Current State

`plugin/bin/verify.js` writes the verification pass stamp for any passing full run regardless of tree state (the write gate "never consults dirty", verify.js ~line 547), and `--stamp-status` reports `verifiedHead: true` only when the stored stamp was recorded against a clean tree at the current HEAD (`stampCoversCleanHead`, verify.js ~line 125). The dirty value comes from `gitInfo()` in `plugin/bin/lib/verify/report.js`.

When a check regenerates a tracked file — the reported case is a Next.js production build rewriting `next-env.d.ts` — the tree is dirty at stamp time even though every check passed on the exact HEAD commit. `--stamp-status` then reads `verifiedHead: false`, `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5 re-triggers `/claude-tweaks:test`, and the re-run dirties the tree again. The only way to a verifying stamp is a second run that leaves the build out, or a manual restore-and-restamp.

A second, smaller gap from the same report: `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` gives no guidance for a `--cmd` that needs environment variables or an interpreter-specific import path; the reporter needed two failed runs to learn that a committed wrapper script must put the working directory first on the import path.

## Deliverables

1. `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` accepts a `generated` list of path globs. `verify.js`'s dirty computation for the pass stamp ignores changes to paths matching those globs; any other dirty path still disqualifies the stamp exactly as today.
2. The stamp records which declared-generated paths were dirty at stamp time, so the exemption is auditable.
3. `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` documents the `generated` key (when to use it, and that it must name only files the checks regenerate) and adds a short note on `--cmd` wrappers needing environment variables or a working-directory-first import path.
4. `/claude-tweaks:init`'s verify-scope starter (`plugin/bin/lib/init/verify-scope-starter.js`) accepts the new key without breaking existing scope files.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A full passing run whose only dirty path matches a declared `generated` glob produces a stamp for which `--stamp-status` reports `verifiedHead: true`, and the stamp lists that path.
2. A full passing run with any other dirty path still produces `verifiedHead: false`.
3. A scope file without `generated` behaves exactly as today.
4. `node --test tests/bin-lib/verify/stamp.test.js` and the verify CLI tests pass, with new cases for 1–3.

## Release Note

Verification can now earn a passing stamp when a check regenerates a declared generated file, instead of forcing a second run.

## Technical Approach

Extend the verify-scope declaration parser to read `generated`, pass the globs into the dirty computation used for the pass stamp (not the general report's `dirty`, which other readers may rely on), and record the exempted paths in the stamp. Option (b) from the original request — exempting any path that was clean before the run and dirtied by it — is rejected: a check that rewrites source (a formatter or `lint --fix`) would then vouch for a tree that differs from HEAD. Explicit declaration keeps that case disqualifying.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — stamp write and `--stamp-status` dirty handling
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/report.js` — `gitInfo()` dirty computation; add a filtered variant for the stamp
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/stamp.js` — record exempted generated paths in the stamp
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/declaration.js` — parse `generated` from `verify-scope.json`
- `plugin/bin/lib/init/verify-scope-starter.js` — starter scope file compatibility
- `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` — document `generated` and the `--cmd` wrapper note
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/stamp.test.js` — new cases

## Gotchas

- #2806 (untangling `verify/args.js`'s parseArgs, PR #2836) is in flight in the same module family; land after it merges or rebase onto it to avoid conflicts.
- #3002 (per-suite stamps for chunked runs) changes the same stamp format; coordinate the stamp schema so both additions compose.
- The stamp's existing semantics (#1921: the runner is the only writer; #1784: no agent-side writes) must not change.

## Original request

bin/verify.js pass stamp: reads dirty when a check regenerates a tracked file

**Component:** `bin/verify.js` pass stamp (`--stamp-status`, `verifiedHead`) and `test/verification.md` "Verification pass stamp", plugin version 6.134.1.

**Kind:** Gap.

**What happened.** A project's full check list includes a production build of a Next.js app. That build rewrites a tracked, generated type-declaration file (`next-env.d.ts`) in place, so the working tree is dirty at the moment `verify.js` writes its pass stamp. Every check passed on the exact HEAD commit, but `--stamp-status` then reports `verifiedHead: false`, and `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5 treats `TEST_PASSED=true` plus a non-verifying stamp as "re-trigger `/claude-tweaks:test`". Re-running the same full set dirties the tree again, so the only way to a verifying stamp is a second run that leaves the build out.

**Why it matters.** The stamp's dirty rule exists to stop a pass on uncommitted source from vouching for a commit. A file the checks themselves regenerate is a different case, and today it forces a redundant run (minutes of wall-clock per review) or a manual restore-and-rerun on every project whose build touches a tracked generated file.

**Suggested behaviour.** One of: (a) let `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` declare `generated` paths the stamp's dirty check ignores; (b) have `verify.js` compare the dirty set before and after the run and treat paths that were clean before the run and dirtied only by the checks as non-disqualifying, recording them in the stamp; or (c) document the workaround in `test/verification.md` (restore the generated file, then re-stamp with a check set that does not regenerate it).

**Second, related observation from the same run.** A project with no `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` and a Python test list that needs environment variables has no documented way to express `--cmd tests=` other than a hand-written wrapper script, and a script-driven test runner resolves the project's packages differently from `python -m pytest` (the script's directory, not the working directory, is first on the import path). A short note in `test/verification.md` — "when `--cmd` needs environment variables or an interpreter-specific import path, commit a wrapper in the project and put the working directory first on the import path" — would have saved two failed verification runs.

Surface: infra

**Related:** #2679 (a practice to re-audit verification prompts on Claude model bumps — adjacent but distinct: that record is about verification-prompt wording specifically, this one is about skill/description trimming)

## Current State

External guidance (attributed to newer-model best-practice advice) argues that skill descriptions should shrink and that pre-reading doc stacks written for older, weaker models should stop, on the premise that a more capable model needs less hand-holding prose to trigger and use a skill correctly. claude-tweaks currently has ~40+ skills, many with substantial `SKILL.md` files and multi-file lazy-loaded sub-documents (per `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s conventions), whose descriptions and content depth have not been audited against this specific guidance.

## Deliverables

Audit a representative sample of claude-tweaks' skill descriptions and frontmatter against the trimming guidance, and produce findings: which descriptions carry verbosity that no longer earns its keep for a newer model, and which genuinely need their current depth (a skill whose triggering accuracy or correctness depends on detailed disambiguation, not verbosity for its own sake). Apply trims only where the finding is clear-cut; leave ambiguous cases as documented findings for a human decision rather than trimming speculatively.

## Acceptance Criteria

- At least a representative sample of skill descriptions/frontmatter (not necessarily all ~40+) is reviewed against the guidance, with findings stated per-skill (trim / keep-as-is / needs-human-judgment), not a blanket assertion.
- Any trims actually applied preserve triggering accuracy — verified by checking the trimmed description still matches this project's own skill-selection conventions (`docs/skill-authoring.md`'s Frontmatter conventions section) and doesn't remove disambiguating detail that exists for a documented reason (e.g. distinguishing near-identical skill names).
- Findings and any applied changes are summarized in the record's own closing report or a linked doc, not left implicit in a diff alone.

## Release Note

Trimmed skill descriptions that no longer help newer models pick the right skill.

## Technical Approach

Read `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s Frontmatter conventions section first to understand this repo's existing description-writing rules before trimming against external guidance — the two may already agree, or the external guidance may conflict with an already-deliberate convention here, in which case that conflict itself is a finding worth stating rather than silently picking one side. Sample a cross-section of skills (a few long-description ones, a few already-terse ones) rather than attempting all ~40+ in one pass, given the record's own scope is an audit, not a mandated full rewrite.

### Key Files

- `docs/skill-authoring.md` — this repo's existing frontmatter/description conventions, the baseline to compare external guidance against
- A sample of `plugin/skills/*/SKILL.md` frontmatter blocks — the actual audit targets (specific files depend on which sample is chosen)

## Gotchas

- Don't trim indiscriminately — a skill's description length sometimes exists specifically to disambiguate from a near-identical skill name or to state a hard trigger condition precisely; removing that in the name of brevity could regress triggering accuracy, which is a worse outcome than the verbosity the record is trying to fix.
- If this repo's own `docs/skill-authoring.md` conventions already conflict with the external trimming guidance, surface that conflict explicitly as a finding rather than silently reconciling it one way — that's a decision for a human, not this shaping pass or the eventual build.

## Original request

Trim skill/AGENTS.md descriptions per newer-model guidance

Context: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra guidance says to shrink skill descriptions and stop pre-reading doc stacks written for older, weaker models.

Scope: Audit claude-tweaks' own skill descriptions and templates against this trimming guidance.
